chunks: From him, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

If a man is struck on his head and his tongue becomes impaired, the letters of the alphabet are presented to him. For whatever of them he cannot articulate, compensation is paid according to that portion of the alphabet. The full diyah is apportioned over the entire alphabet, and he is given compensation in proportion to what he cannot articulate of it, and they are twenty-nine letters.

key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: the prescribed financial compensation for bodily injury
key_terms.بِحِسَابِ: in proportion or according to calculation
key_terms.تِسْعَةٌ وَعِشْرُونَ حَرْفًا: twenty-nine letters, the total count used for calculation
key_terms.ثَقُلَ لِسَانُهُ: his tongue became impaired or heavy in speech
key_terms.حُرُوفُ الْمُعْجَمِ: the letters of the alphabet used to assess speech ability

ai.seo_question: How is diyah calculated in Shia fiqh for speech impairment caused by a head injury?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal method for assessing diyah when a head injury causes impairment of speech. The compensation is calculated proportionally by testing the injured person against the letters of the alphabet and assigning liability according to the letters he can no longer articulate.
